title: Dispatch: olc5.12 repair Sol r1 S1-S7 (grant identity, concentration, presence, timing, refresh, goat, resolver) (attempt 3)
description:
Repair attempt 3 for capability eshyra-olc5.12 after the Sol final review of PR #665. Read ALL findings S1-S7 in `bd show eshyra-olc5.12.5` first (each has location, failure probe, required closure and permanent-evidence guidance). Also read eshyra-olc5.12.1 / .12.2 notes. Branch eshyra-olc5.12.6 cut from eshyra-olc5.12 @ b205724d. Fix every finding in ONE batch, including siblings of each (same defect class on other carriers/paths). Importer work follows docs/importer-fix-protocol.md; regenerate the pack and confirm npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack.

CAPTAIN DECISIONS (follow; if one is wrong against source or code, STOP and report in notes):

S1 identity. (a) Pack: grants of a variant-bearing item must name the variant(s) they belong to. Add an optional typed `variants: string[]` (variant ids exactly as the item's variant records/ids use them) to entityGrant grants, authored in magicItemEntityGrants.ts for Figurine of Wondrous Power from the source variant headings (Bronze Griffon -> bronze-griffon grant, ..., Ivory Goats -> the three goat grants, etc.; check the real variant ids in the generated record). Schema-validate: each listed variant must exist on the item; for an item that HAS variants, every grant must list variants (fail pack load otherwise). (b) Runtime: binding requires the instance's variant_id to be in grant.variants when the item has variants; an instance with no variant on a variant-bearing item refuses. (c) Any source carrying grantRef or itemInstanceId must be kind 'magic-item' with a ref that resolves; unknown grant refuses; no path may leave a declared grantRef unbound (item_grant_json NULL). Fix both validators (activeEffects.ts createActiveEffect and toolStartEffect.ts) so neither skips when ref is absent.

S2 concentration, derived from the grant. Rule per grant: (i) grant.control is 'as spell:<ref>' (elemental vessels, Elemental Gem): concentration REQUIRED (concentrationOwner must be given) and the break behaviour is that spell's: extend createUncontrolledSuccessor (activeEffects.ts ~L3084, currently spell-only) so a grant-bound effect whose grant control names a spell uses that spell record's deriveUncontrolledRemoval (the elemental stays, uncontrolled, and disappears at the spell's deadline measured from the original summon). Do not hand-code conjure-elemental; resolve the spell named by the pointer. (ii) revertOn contains 'concentration-ended' (Ring of Djinni): concentration REQUIRED; break removes the creature (ordinary). (iii) otherwise: concentration FORBIDDEN (refuse a concentrationOwner), e.g. Figurines. Tool text states the rule.

S3 presence. For grant-bound linked actors, the printed ending removes the creature: refuse cleanupOnEnd/cleanupOnBreak 'release' (or any non-removing policy) and default them to the removing policy, except the S2(i) exceptional break path which hands the creature to the uncontrolled successor. Every grant-ended anchor emission must coincide with the creature leaving play. A dm-override/house-rule duration does not license a non-removing policy.

S4 timing. Carry the effective termination minute (the effect's deadline for expiry; the event time for cascaded endings; the current clock for explicit end) into applyItemCooldownAnchorEvent so availableAt = termination + cooldown, and ensure a clock advance that crosses both the effect deadline and the resulting availableAt settles the item reset within the same advance (check ordering in rest.ts / advanceWorldTime and the item reset sweep). Permanent evidence: partition invariance for Ring and Efreeti (one large advance == advances split at the effect deadline and at availableAt).

S5 refresh. refresh_effect on a grant-bound effect revalidates the duration exactly like creation: typed fixed duration must stay equal with typed-fixed provenance; a different amount/unit/kind requires an explicit dm-override (basis + reason), recorded as unbound provenance replacing the stale typed-fixed record. Same for item-effect (effectRef) bindings if they share the defect.

S6 goat. A 'timer' disposition with NO typed duration (goat-of-traveling: charge-driven lifetime) accepts a DM-supplied timed duration recorded as unbound/dm-adjudicated (the existing itemDurationBinding unbound status) and does not invent a cap; until-removed is also admissible there with the DM ending it by end_effect. Verify every kept timer disposition carrier in the pack can actually bind (admissibility check over all grants, not just key membership).

S7 resolver. Propagate the campaign CampaignRulesPackResolver through every terminal/cascade caller that now consults item mechanics (rest.ts expireElapsedWorldEffects ~L216, round expiry, 0-HP life events, concentration breaks, encounter closure) and make the grant-ended lookup skip resolving item mechanics for grants that have no anchor without needing the whole stack only if that is cheaper; real refusals must still roll back atomically. Permanent evidence: add-on stack parity across explicit end, expiry and life-event endings.

Tests: one generalized test per finding as Sol's required closure describes (invariants over real pack carriers, not only one example), in packages/core/test/itemGrantSummons.test.ts or a sibling file. Keep all existing tests passing; do not weaken any.

Run npm run verify:worktree before committing. Completion notes: per-finding fix + evidence test names, pack diff summary, verify result.

S6 goat: untyped timer grant takes dm-override timed duration or until-removed; printed fixed timer constrains amount. Tests: 'S6 goat', 'S6 admissibility'.
S7 resolver: rest advance forwards resolver; DomainMutationContext carries it to HP tools; unanchored grants skip item lookup (cooldownAnchored flag). Tests: 'S7 rules stack', 'S7 anchored Ring on an add-on stack'.

DEVIATIONS / RESIDUALS (not completed, filed as follow-ups): (1) S4 cascaded endings use the current clock, not the cascade event time. (2) S7 resolver forwarding audited for main paths, not proven exhaustive. (3) Ebony Fly acceptance path untested (no creature:giant-fly). Golden Lions count 1 is the faithful-lifecycle design, not a defect.
